slides.title: SEMICOLON OR COLON? HERE'S THE RULE
THE TWO RULES
lines: Semicolon: joins two complete sentences that are closely related.
Colon: introduces a list, explanation, or example after a complete sentence.
slides.note: Both need a complete sentence on the left.

slides.title: SEMICOLON
slides.problem: I studied all night; the test was still hard.
steps: Test: could each side stand alone as a sentence?
Yes, so a semicolon can join them

slides.title: COLON
slides.problem: Bring three things: a pencil, a calculator, and ID.
steps: Left side is a complete sentence
The right side lists what 'three things' means

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: I need: a pencil and paper.
points: Don't put a colon right after a verb or 'such as'. The left side isn't a complete sentence.
Fix: I need a pencil and paper.

pageTitle: Semicolons vs Colons: Rules and Common Mistakes
description: Learn when to use a semicolon and when to use a colon, with simple tests and example sentences.
